    36:     url_username: "{{ ucs_dns_dnsserver_user }}"
    37:     url_password: "{{ ucs_dns_dnsserver_password }}"
    38:     method: PUT

    40:     status_code:
    41:       - 200
    42:       - 204
    43:     body:
    44:       position: "{{ ucs_dns_ldap_zone }}"
    45:       properties:

    47:         zonettl: "{{ usc_dns_ttl_in_seconds }}"

    57:   delegate_to: localhost
    58:   changed_when: true
    59: 
    60: - name: Create entry

    62:     headers:
    63:       Accept: application/json
    64:     url: https://{{ ucs_dns_dnsserver }}/univention/udm/dns/host_record/
    65:     url_username: "{{ ucs_dns_dnsserver_user }}"
    66:     url_password: "{{ ucs_dns_dnsserver_password }}"

name: utils/nist_sync/ansible/setup.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact overly complex because several size and dependency dimensions compound?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # One-time setup of the RHEL9 scanner VM.
     3: #
     4: # Usage (from utils/nist_sync/):
     5: #   ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory.ini ansible/setup.yml \
     6: #     -e complyctl_bin=/tmp/complyctl \
     7: #     -e provider_bin=~/.complytime/providers/complyctl-provider-openscap
     8: #
     9: # Optional env overrides (also accepted as -e vars):
    10: #   COMPLYCTL_BIN   path to complyctl binary on the host  (default: /tmp/complyctl)
    11: #   PROVIDER_BIN    path to complyctl-provider-openscap   (default: ~/.complytime/providers/...)
    12: #   ORAS_VERSION    oras release to install               (default: 1.2.3)
    13: #   REGISTRY_PORT   container registry port inside the VM (default: 5500)
    14: 
    15: - name: Set up complyctl NIST scanner on RHEL9
    16:   hosts: rhel9_scanner
    17:   become: true
    18:   vars:
    19:     complyctl_bin: "{{ lookup('env', 'COMPLYCTL_BIN') | default('/tmp/complyctl', true) }}"
    20:     provider_bin: "{{ lookup('env', 'PROVIDER_BIN') | default(ansible_env.HOME + '/.complytime/providers/complyctl-provider-openscap', true) }}"
    21:     oras_version: "{{ lookup('env', 'ORAS_VERSION') | default('1.2.3', true) }}"
    22:     registry_port: "{{ lookup('env', 'REGISTRY_PORT')  | default('5500', true) }}"
    23:     # Root of the content repo on the host — three levels above the playbook dir.
    24:     # playbook_dir = .../utils/nist_sync/ansible
    25:     repo_root: "{{ playbook_dir | realpath + '/../../..' }}"
    26:     ds_dest: /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml
    27: 
    28:   tasks:
    29:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    30:     # complyctl binary
    31:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    32:     - name: Copy complyctl binary
    33:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    34:         src: "{{ complyctl_bin }}"
    35:         dest: /usr/local/bin/complyctl
    36:         mode: "0755"
    37: 
    38:     - name: Verify complyctl runs
    39:       ansible.builtin.command: /usr/local/bin/complyctl version
    40:       register: ver
    41:       changed_when: false
    42: 
    43:     - name: Show complyctl version
    44:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    45:         msg: "{{ ver.stdout }}"
    46: 
    47:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48:     # complyctl-provider-openscap
    49:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    50:     - name: Create provider directory
    51:       ansible.builtin.file:
    52:         path: /root/.local/share/complytime/providers
    53:         state: directory
    54:         mode: "0755"
    55: 
    56:     - name: Copy complyctl-provider-openscap
    57:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    58:         src: "{{ provider_bin }}"
    59:         dest: /root/.local/share/complytime/providers/complyctl-provider-openscap
    60:         mode: "0755"
    61: 
    62:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    63:     # OCI registry — distribution/distribution binary (no podman required).
    64:     # Runs as a systemd service inside the VM listening on all interfaces.
    65:     # The host pushes bundles to ansible_host:{{ registry_port }} via oras;
    66:     # complyctl on the VM uses http://localhost:{{ registry_port }}.
    67:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    68:     - name: Check if registry binary is already installed
    69:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    70:         path: /usr/local/bin/registry
    71:       register: registry_bin_stat
    72: 
    73:     - name: Download distribution/distribution registry binary
    74:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
    75:         curl -sL \
    76:           "https://github.com/distribution/distribution/releases/download/v2.8.3/registry_2.8.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz" \
    77:           | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin registry
    78:         chmod +x /usr/local/bin/registry
    79:       when: not registry_bin_stat.stat.exists
    80: 
    81:     - name: Create registry storage directory
    82:       ansible.builtin.file:
    83:         path: /var/lib/gemara-registry
    84:         state: directory
    85:         mode: "0755"
    86: 
    87:     - name: Write registry config
    88:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    89:         dest: /etc/gemara-registry.yml
    90:         mode: "0644"
    91:         content: |
    92:           version: 0.1
    93:           log:
    94:             level: warn
    95:           storage:
    96:             filesystem:
    97:               rootdirectory: /var/lib/gemara-registry
    98:             delete:
    99:               enabled: true
   100:           http:
   101:             addr: :{{ registry_port }}
   102: 
   103:     - name: Create systemd service for registry
   104:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   105:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/gemara-registry.service
   106:         mode: "0644"
   107:         content: |
   108:           [Unit]
   109:           Description=Gemara OCI Registry
   110:           After=network.target
   111:           [Service]
   112:           ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/registry serve /etc/gemara-registry.yml
   113:           Restart=always
   114:           RestartSec=3
   115:           [Install]
   116:           WantedBy=multi-user.target
   117: 
   118:     - name: Enable and start registry service
   119:       ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   120:         name: gemara-registry
   121:         state: started
   122:         enabled: true
   123:         daemon_reload: true
   124: 
   125:     - name: Wait for registry to become ready
   126:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   127:         url: "http://localhost:{{ registry_port }}/v2/"
   128:         status_code: 200
   129:       retries: 15
   130:       delay: 2
   131:       register: registry_ready
   132:       until: registry_ready.status == 200
   133: 
   134:     - name: Registry is ready
   135:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   136:         msg: "OCI registry running at localhost:{{ registry_port }} (and {{ ansible_host }}:{{ registry_port }} from the host)"
   137: 
   138:     - name: Open registry port in the VM firewall
   139:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
   140:         firewall-cmd --add-port={{ registry_port }}/tcp --permanent
   141:         firewall-cmd --reload
   142:       args:
   143:         executable: /bin/bash
   144:       changed_when: true
   145: 
   146:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147:     # SCAP data stream — always copy the repo-built version.
   148:     # The system RPM (scap-security-guide) predates the nist_800_53 profile
   149:     # commit and will not contain that profile.  The built data stream must
   150:     # be deployed even if the RPM is already installed.
   151:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   152:     - name: "Copy built data stream from host"
   153:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   154:         src: "{{ repo_root }}/build/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml"
   155:         dest: "{{ ds_dest }}"
   156:         mode: "0644"
   157:         force: true
   158: 
   159:     - name: Confirm data stream has nist_800_53 profile
   160:       ansible.builtin.command: "grep -c nist_800_53 {{ ds_dest }}"
   161:       register: profile_check
   162:       changed_when: false
   163:       failed_when: profile_check.rc != 0 or profile_check.stdout | int == 0
   164: 
   165:     - name: Show data stream status
   166:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   167:         msg: "Data stream: {{ ds_dest }} — nist_800_53 profile present ({{ profile_check.stdout }} occurrences)"
   168: 
   169:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   170:     # Summary
   171:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   172:     - name: Setup complete
   173:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   174:         msg: |
   175:           VM is ready. Run the scan with:
   176:             ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory.ini ansible/scan.yml

    26: # Note that the handler must do a restart instead of a reload as some of
    27: #  these defaults are only read at startup
    28: - name: Create defaults for dnsmasq used when starting dnsmasq (including not adding the local machine as a resolver)
    29:   copy:
    30:     src: etc_default_dnsmasq
    31:     dest: /etc/default/dnsmasq
    32: 
    33: # This is necessary because nginx redirects to the hostname, but the hostname
    34: #  is listed in /etc/hosts and associated with 127.0.0.1 (so dnsmasq uses it
    35: #  when answering queries). By adding this, and the localise-queries option
    36: #  to dnsmasq, we answer with the address of the wifi interface. There's no
    37: #  need to do this for the ethernet interface, as we're not answering queries
    38: #  on that interface (we're not even listening)
    39: - name: Add /etc/hosts entry for wifi interface

    57: - name: Install dnsmasq

1: # skip restart if the operator deferred restarts LFOps-wide (lfops__skip_restart_handlers), if
     2: # the service was just started (redundant), or if the user wants it stopped.
     3: # __elasticsearch__service_state_result is registered on a dedicated state-only task (not the
     4: # enabled task), so that enabled-only changes don't prevent the restart.

     6: # where the result is never registered.

    11:   when:

    13:     - '__elasticsearch__service_state_result is not defined or __elasticsearch__service_state_result is not changed'

     9: - block:
    10: 
    11:   - name: 'Install php php-fpm composer'
    12:     ansible.builtin.package:
    13:       name: '{{ __php__base_packages }}'
    14:       state: 'present'
    15: 
    16:   tags:
    17:     - 'php'
    18:

    20: - block:
    21: 
    22:   # refresh the apt cache so the following `state: latest` upgrade resolves
    23:   # against current metadata, e.g. to roll out security updates. apt does not
    24:   # auto-expire its cache the way dnf does, so without this the upgrade can
    25:   # silently run against a stale cache and miss newer versions.
    26:   - name: 'apt update # update the cache'
    27:     ansible.builtin.apt:
    28:       update_cache: true
    29:     changed_when: false # refreshing the package cache is not a config change
    30:     when: 'ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"'
    31: 
    32:   # On Debian with php__version set, the package names carry the declared version, so this task
    33:   # installs the new stack as soon as the user raises php__version. That is deliberate: pinning the
    34:   # version makes a major change explicit, it does not make it impossible. Without php__version the
    35:   # unversioned metapackages are updated exactly as before.
    36:   - name: 'Update php php-fpm composer' # noqa package-latest (we explicitly want latest here)
    37:     ansible.builtin.package:
    38:       name: '{{ __php__base_packages }}'
    39:       state: 'latest'
    40:     notify: 'php: php-fpm --test; restart php-fpm'
    41: 
    42:   tags:
    43:     - 'never'
    44:     - 'php:update'
    45: 
    46: 
    47: - block:
    48: 
    49:   - name: 'Get the list of installed packages'
    50:     ansible.builtin.package_facts:  # yamllint disable-line rule:empty-values
    51:     check_mode: false # run task even if `--check` is specified
    52: 
    53:   # php__version wins when set: the role then manages exactly the declared version instead of
    54:   # adopting whatever happens to be installed. Falling back to discovery keeps the previous
    55:   # behaviour, and is the only option on RedHat, where the 'php' package always exists.
    56:   - name: 'Get PHP version'
    57:     ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    58:       __php__installed_version: '{{
    59:           php__version if (php__version | string | length)
    60:           else (ansible_facts["packages"]["php"][0]["version"] | regex_search("\d\.\d"))

   273:   # updates around forever. Purging runs last, after the new version's config, pools and service

   298:       state: 'absent'
   299:       purge: true

   304:     - 'php__version | string | length > 0'

    12:         seconds: 5

    23:         # When status.conditions[x].type == Ready then check stats.conditions[x].status for True|False
    24:         - kubectl_get_node['stdout'] | from_json | json_query("status.conditions[?type == 'Ready'].status")

     2: # This task is used to create variables used in giving a warning summary for manual tasks

     4: #
     5: # The warn_control_list and warn_count vars start life in vars/main.yml but get updated
     6: # as the tasks that have a warning complete
     7: #
     8: # Those two variables are used in the tasks/main.yml to display a list of warnings
     9: #
    10: # warn_control_id is set within the task itself and has the control ID as the value

    12: # warn_control_list is the main variable to be used and is a list made up of the warn_control_id’s

    16: - name: "{{ warn_control_id }} | WARNING | Set fact for manual task warning." # noqa name[template]
    17:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    18:     warn_control_list: "{{ warn_control_list }} [{{ warn_control_id }}]"
    19:     warn_count: "{{ warn_count | int + 1 }}"

   127: 
   128: - name: Render Docker-Compose

     2: # This playbook performs a rollback of a PostgreSQL database cluster upgrade.
     3: # It's designed to be used when a PostgreSQL upgrade hasn't been fully completed and the new version hasn't been started.
     4: # The rollback operation is performed by starting the Patroni cluster with the old version of PostgreSQL using the same PGDATA.
     5: # The playbook first checks the health of the current cluster, verifies the version of PostgreSQL, and ensures the new PostgreSQL is not running.
     6: # If these checks pass, the playbook switches back to the old PostgreSQL paths and restarts the Patroni service.
     7: # Notes:
     8: # If pg_upgrade aborted before linking started, the old cluster was unmodified; it can be restarted.
     9: # If you did not start the new cluster, the old cluster was unmodified except that,
    10: # when linking started, a .old suffix was appended to $PGDATA/global/pg_control.
    11: # To reuse the old cluster, remove the .old suffix from $PGDATA/global/pg_control; you can then restart the old cluster.
    12: # If you did start the new cluster, it has written to shared files and it is unsafe to use the old cluster.
    13: # The old cluster will need to be restored from backup in this case.
    14: 
    15: # If the cluster is already healthy, the process stops to avoid unnecessary actions.
    16: - name: "[Rollback] Check Patroni cluster state"
    17:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    18:     url: "{{ patroni_restapi_protocol }}://{{ patroni_restapi_connect_addr | default(patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true), true) }}:\
    19:       {{ patroni_restapi_port }}/cluster"
    20:     return_content: true
    21:     ca_path: "{{ patroni_restapi_cafile | default(omit, true) }}"
    22:   register: patroni_cluster_result
    23:   failed_when: false
    24:   changed_when: false
    25:   environment:
    26:     no_proxy: "{{ patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true) }}"
    27:   when:
    28:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
    29: 
    30: # Stop, if the Patroni cluster is already healthy
    31: - name: "[Rollback] Abort if the Patroni cluster is already running"
    32:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    33:     msg: "The Patroni cluster is already running. Stop rollback."
    34:   vars:
    35:     cluster_members: "{{ patroni_cluster_result.json.members | default([]) | rejectattr('state', 'equalto', 'stopped') | list | length }}"
    36:     total_nodes: "{{ groups['primary'] | length + groups.get('secondary', []) | length }}"
    37:   when:
    38:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
    39:     # Check if the cluster members (excluding 'stopped') equals the total number of nodes
    40:     - cluster_members == total_nodes
    41: 
    42: - name: "[Rollback] Make sure the new PostgreSQL is not running"
    43:   ansible.builtin.command: "{{ pg_new_bindir }}/pg_ctl status -D {{ pg_new_datadir }}"
    44:   register: pg_ctl_status_new_result
    45:   failed_when: false
    46:   changed_when: false

    55:     - pg_ctl_status_new_result is defined
    56:     - pg_ctl_status_new_result.rc == 0

    67:   when: pg_control_old.stat.exists

   152:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']

   156:   become_user: root

    15:     - name: dashboards <|> Download grafana dashboard from grafana.net to local directory # noqa command-instead-of-module

    20:       args:

    22:       register: grafana_download_dashboards

    24:       retries: 5
    25:       delay: 2

1: ---
     2: # Purpose: Refresh interface facts for the host currently being processed.
     3: # Re-reads /machines/ from MAAS via _read_machines.yml + _build_indexes.yml,
     4: # then narrows down to this host's interfaces and rebuilds the per-host
     5: # quick-lookup maps used by _apply_one_iface.yml and _ensure_bond.yml.
     6: #
     7: # Expects:
     8: #   - host : short hostname (used as the key into maas_host_to_ifaces)
     9: #   - _maas_api, maas_auth_header
    10: # Returns:
    11: #   - _ifaces             : list of MAAS interface objects for this host
    12: #   - _iface_by_name      : { name → iface_obj }
    13: #   - _iface_id_by_name   : { name → id }
    14: #   - _iface_id_by_mac    : { mac (lowered) → id }
    15: #   - _existing_vlan_pairs: VLAN-subinterface index keyed by parent
    16: #   - _native_by_parent   : { parent_id → native vlan_id|None }
    17: # Side effects: GET {{ _maas_api }}/machines/ (via _read_machines.yml).
    18: 
    19: - include_tasks: _read_machines.yml
    20: 
    21: - include_tasks: _build_indexes.yml
    22: 
    23: - name: Set raw interface list
    24:   set_fact:
    25:     _ifaces: "{{ maas_host_to_ifaces[host] }}"
    26: 
    27: # 2) Rebuild quick lookups
    28: - name: Build interface lookup maps (by name, by id, by mac)
    29:   set_fact:
    30:     _iface_by_name: >-
    31:       {{
    32:         dict(
    33:           (_ifaces | map(attribute='name') | list)
    34:           | zip(_ifaces | list)
    35:         )
    36:       }}
    37:     _iface_id_by_name: >-
    38:       {{
    39:         dict(
    40:           (_ifaces | map(attribute='name') | list)
    41:           | zip(_ifaces | map(attribute='id') | list)
    42:         )
    43:       }}
    44:     _iface_id_by_mac: >-
    45:       {{
    46:         dict(
    47:           (
    48:             _ifaces
    49:             | selectattr('mac_address','defined')
    50:             | map(attribute='mac_address')
    51:             | map('lower')
    52:             | list
    53:           )
    54:           | zip(
    55:               _ifaces
    56:               | selectattr('mac_address','defined')
    57:               | map(attribute='id')
    58:               | list
    59:             )
    60:         )
    61:       }}
    62: 
    63: # 3) Index existing VLAN subinterfaces as (parent_id, vlan_id) pairs

    65:   set_fact:
    66:     _existing_vlan_pairs: []
    67: 
    68: - name: Build existing VLAN pair index
    69:   set_fact:
    70:     _existing_vlan_pairs: >-
    71:       {{
    72:         _existing_vlan_pairs + [ {
    73:           'parent_id': (_iface_id_by_name.get(item.parents[0]) | int),
    74:           'vlan_id': item.vlan.id,
    75:           'iface_id': item.id,
    76:           'name': item.name
    77:         } ]
    78:       }}
    79:   loop: "{{ _ifaces | selectattr('type','equalto','vlan') | list }}"
    80:   when:
    81:     - item.parents is defined
    82:     - (item.parents | length) > 0
    83:     - item.vlan is defined
    84:     - item.vlan.id is defined
    85:   loop_control:
    86:     label: "{{ item.name | default(item.id) }}"

    90:   set_fact:
    91:     _native_by_parent: {}
    92:

    96:   loop: "{{ _ifaces | rejectattr('type','equalto','vlan') | list }}"

name: roles/postgres/tasks/main/pg_dump_backups.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact overly complex because several size and dependency dimensions compound?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # =============================================================================
     3: # Phase 5: pg_dump backups on the persistent mount, via a systemd timer
     4: # =============================================================================
     5: - name: Configure pg_dump backups
     6:   when: postgres_backup_enabled | bool
     7:   block:
     8:     - name: Create the backup directory on the persistent mount
     9:       ansible.builtin.file:
    10:         path: "{{ postgres_backup_dir }}"
    11:         state: directory
    12:         owner: postgres
    13:         group: postgres
    14:         mode: "0750"
    15: 
    16:     - name: Deploy the pg_dump backup script
    17:       ansible.builtin.template:
    18:         src: pg-backup.sh.j2
    19:         dest: /usr/local/bin/pg-backup.sh
    20:         owner: root
    21:         group: root
    22:         mode: "0755"
    23: 
    24:     - name: Deploy the pg_dump backup systemd service
    25:       ansible.builtin.template:
    26:         src: pg-backup.service.j2
    27:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/pg-backup.service
    28:         owner: root
    29:         group: root
    30:         mode: "0644"
    31: 
    32:     - name: Deploy the pg_dump backup systemd timer
    33:       ansible.builtin.template:
    34:         src: pg-backup.timer.j2
    35:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/pg-backup.timer
    36:         owner: root
    37:         group: root
    38:         mode: "0644"
    39: 
    40:     - name: Enable and start the pg_dump backup timer
    41:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    42:         name: pg-backup.timer
    43:         state: started
    44:         enabled: true
    45:         daemon_reload: true
    46: 
    47: # Trust the standby node's puller so ansible-proxmox roles/postgres_standby can
    48: # rsync the backup directory into the replicated archive (Tier 1 of the
    49: # Database DR Standard). Env-gated: no key supplied, no trust installed.
    50: #
    51: # rrsync is the forced command rather than a pinned `rsync --server --sender`
    52: # argv: the argv the client sends changes with rsync's flags, so pinning it
    53: # breaks the pull silently on an upgrade. rrsync ships in the rsync package.
    54: #
    55: # Both tasks also carry their own tag so the trust can be (re)applied on its
    56: # own — rotating a puller's key should not require converging the whole
    57: # engine on a live database guest:
    58: #
    59: #   --tags postgres_standby_trust -e postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys="$(...)"
    60: #
    61: # Pass the keys as an EXTRA VAR, not an exported environment variable.
    62: # `VAR=x doppler run -- ...` does not override a Doppler-managed variable —
    63: # Doppler's injected value wins over the caller's export, silently — so an
    64: # export is ignored and whatever the secret holds is authorized instead, at
    65: # rc=0 with changed=true. The default binding no longer reads any env var
    66: # (it fed the stale pve2 puller key on every converge); an extra var is the
    67: # only resolution path.
    68: - name: Install rsync for the standby puller's forced command
    69:   ansible.builtin.apt:
    70:     name: rsync
    71:     state: present
    72:   when: postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys | length > 0
    73:   tags:
    74:     - postgres_standby_trust
    75: 
    76: - name: Authorize the standby puller's SSH key(s) for root
    77:   ansible.posix.authorized_key:
    78:     user: root
    79:     key: "{{ postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys }}"
    80:     # The puller anchors its source path at "/" — rrsync resolves that to this
    81:     # directory. An absolute path would be prefixed with it and match nothing.
    82:     key_options: 'restrict,command="rrsync -ro {{ postgres_backup_dir }}"'
    83:   when: postgres_standby_pull_pubkeys | length > 0
    84:   tags:
    85:     - postgres_standby_trust
    86: 
    87: # Declared state includes the absence: the decommissioned pve2 puller's key
    88: # (forced rrsync command, comment root@pve2) was re-authorised by every
    89: # converge while the env binding above still fed the stale Doppler secret
    90: # (Zammad #17250). Not gated on pubkeys — this scrubs even when no puller is
    91: # being trusted, and matches only that puller's line so human and current
    92: # puller keys are untouched. The current pullers' keys carry the
    93: # postgres-standby-pull comment instead.
    94: - name: Remove trust for the decommissioned pve2 backup puller
    95:   ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    96:     path: /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
    97:     regexp: 'rrsync -ro .*\broot@pve2$'
    98:     state: absent
    99:   tags:
   100:     - postgres_standby_trust

name: roles/traefik/tasks/main.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact overly complex because several size and dependency dimensions compound?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # traefik — install the static binary under systemd, render the static + dynamic
     3: # config, and let Traefik fetch/renew a wildcard cert via Route53 DNS-01 itself.
     4: # Render is always done; the binary download + systemd start are gated on
     5: # traefik_manage_services (false in CI/template-render — no live ACME).
     6: 
     7: # --- Fail fast on a real run with missing creds / base domain ----------------
     8: - name: Assert Route53 DNS-01 credentials + ingress base domain are present (live run)
     9:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    10:     that:
    11:       - traefik_acme_aws_access_key_id | length > 0
    12:       - traefik_acme_aws_secret_access_key | length > 0
    13:       - traefik_acme_route53_zone_id | length > 0
    14:       - traefik_base_domain | length > 0
    15:     fail_msg: >-
    16:       Traefik needs the dedicated `acme` AWS user's Route53 DNS-01 credentials and
    17:       the ingress base domain. Set AWS_ACME_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_ACME_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    18:       + PROXMOX_SUBDOMAIN in Doppler and ensure ROUTE53_ZONE_ID is
    19:       set (reused from aws-infra). Attach the least-privilege IAM policy from
    20:       roles/traefik/README.md to that user. Values are never committed.
    21:     quiet: true
    22:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
    23: 
    24: # --- Service account + filesystem layout -------------------------------------
    25: - name: Create traefik group
    26:   ansible.builtin.group:
    27:     name: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    28:     system: true
    29:     state: present
    30: 
    31: - name: Create traefik system user
    32:   ansible.builtin.user:
    33:     name: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    34:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    35:     system: true
    36:     shell: /usr/sbin/nologin
    37:     home: "{{ traefik_config_dir }}"
    38:     create_home: false
    39:     state: present
    40: 
    41: - name: Create Traefik config directories
    42:   ansible.builtin.file:
    43:     path: "{{ item }}"
    44:     state: directory
    45:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    46:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    47:     mode: "0750"
    48:   loop:
    49:     - "{{ traefik_config_dir }}"
    50:     - "{{ traefik_dynamic_dir }}"
    51:     - "{{ traefik_acme_dir }}"
    52: 
    53: # acme.json must be 0600 or Traefik refuses to use it.
    54: - name: Ensure acme.json storage exists with strict perms
    55:   ansible.builtin.file:
    56:     path: "{{ traefik_acme_storage }}"
    57:     state: touch
    58:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    59:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    60:     mode: "0600"
    61:     modification_time: preserve
    62:     access_time: preserve
    63: 
    64: # --- Credentials (root-only EnvironmentFile) ---------------------------------
    65: - name: Render the Route53 DNS-01 credentials EnvironmentFile
    66:   ansible.builtin.template:
    67:     src: acme.env.j2
    68:     dest: "{{ traefik_acme_env_file }}"
    69:     owner: root
    70:     group: root
    71:     mode: "0600"
    72:   no_log: true
    73:   notify: Restart traefik
    74: 
    75: # --- Static + dynamic config -------------------------------------------------
    76: - name: Render the static Traefik config
    77:   ansible.builtin.template:
    78:     src: traefik.yml.j2
    79:     dest: "{{ traefik_config_dir }}/traefik.yml"
    80:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
    81:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
    82:     mode: "0640"
    83:   notify: Restart traefik
    84: 
    85: # Build the routers from the single tofu-owned ingress table
    86: # (tofu_data.ingress via traefik_ingress_routes). Single-backend rows are
    87: # {name, ip, port}; the Proxmox cluster-UI apex row is {name, apex, backends[],
    88: # port} — a load-balanced pool over the node FQDNs. Optional per row: scheme
    89: # (default http), insecure_tls (self-signed backend, e.g. Splunk / Proxmox),
    90: # sticky + health_check (pool session affinity + per-node health checks). Every
    91: # row is normalised here to {name, fqdn, path_prefix, priority, servers[],
    92: # scheme, insecure_tls, sticky, health_check, sso} so the template stays dumb
    93: # (and fixture-testable):
    94: #   - fqdn    = base domain itself when apex, else <hostname>.<base domain>
    95: #   - servers = one <scheme>://<host-or-ip>:<port> url per backend (or the
    96: #               single ip), so single and multi-backend rows render uniformly.
    97: - name: Build Traefik routers from the inventory ingress table
    98:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    99:     traefik_routes: >-
   100:       {{
   101:         traefik_routes | default([]) + [{
   102:           'name': item.name,
   103:           'fqdn': (item.apex | default(false)) | ternary(
   104:                     traefik_base_domain,
   105:                     (item.hostname | default(item.name, true)) ~ '.' ~ traefik_base_domain),
   106:           'path_prefix': item.path_prefix | default('', true),
   107:           'priority': item.priority | default(0, true),
   108:           'servers': (item.backends | default([item.ip | default('')]))
   109:                      | map('regex_replace', '^', (item.scheme | default('http')) ~ '://')
   110:                      | map('regex_replace', '$', ':' ~ (item.port | string))
   111:                      | list,
   112:           'scheme': item.scheme | default('http'),
   113:           'insecure_tls': item.insecure_tls | default(false),
   114:           'sticky': item.sticky | default(false),
   115:           'health_check': item.health_check | default(false),
   116:           'health_check_path': item.health_check_path | default('/'),
   117:           'health_check_port': item.health_check_port | default(0),
   118:           'health_check_interval': item.health_check_interval
   119:             | default(traefik_health_check_interval_overrides[item.name] | default(''), true)
   120:             | default(traefik_health_check_interval, true),
   121:           'health_check_timeout': item.health_check_timeout | default(traefik_health_check_timeout, true),
   122:           'sso': item.sso | default(false)
   123:         }]
   124:       }}
   125:   loop: "{{ traefik_ingress_routes }}"
   126:   loop_control:
   127:     label: "{{ item.name }} -> {{ (item.backends | default([item.ip | default('?')])) | join(', ') }}:{{ item.port }}"
   128: 
   129: - name: Render the dynamic Traefik config (routers + services)
   130:   ansible.builtin.template:
   131:     src: dynamic.yml.j2
   132:     dest: "{{ traefik_dynamic_dir }}/dynamic.yml"
   133:     owner: "{{ traefik_user }}"
   134:     group: "{{ traefik_group }}"
   135:     mode: "0640"
   136:   notify: Restart traefik
   137: 
   138: # --- Dashboard credentials + binary + service (live runs only) ---------------
   139: # Generate the dashboard basicAuth htpasswd on the host (build-time, persisted,
   140: # idempotent) so no credential is ever committed or in the rendered config.
   141: - name: Generate the dashboard basicAuth credentials
   142:   ansible.builtin.import_tasks: dashboard_auth.yml
   143:   when:
   144:     - traefik_manage_services | bool
   145:     - traefik_dashboard_enabled | bool
   146: 
   147: - name: Install the Traefik binary
   148:   ansible.builtin.import_tasks: install.yml
   149:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   150: 
   151: - name: Render the Traefik systemd unit
   152:   ansible.builtin.template:
   153:     src: traefik.service.j2
   154:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/traefik.service
   155:     owner: root
   156:     group: root
   157:     mode: "0644"
   158:   notify: Restart traefik
   159:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   160: 
   161: - name: Enable + start Traefik
   162:   ansible.builtin.systemd:
   163:     name: traefik.service
   164:     state: started
   165:     enabled: true
   166:     daemon_reload: true
   167:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   168: 
   169: # --- Post-deploy: verify Traefik actually ACCEPTED the dynamic config --------
   170: # Traefik's file provider hot-reloads dynamic.yml and, on a parse/build error,
   171: # logs it and SILENTLY KEEPS THE LAST-GOOD CONFIG (or none) — every backing
   172: # host then 404s with no signal. A rendered config that CI's YAML-parse guard
   173: # somehow still let through (or an env-specific breakage) would otherwise land
   174: # live and stay invisible until someone notices the outage. Flush the pending
   175: # restart, then fail the converge loudly if the file provider rejected the
   176: # config, instead of reporting a green run over a dead ingress.
   177: - name: Apply the pending Traefik restart before verifying the config loaded
   178:   ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   179: 
   180: - name: Give Traefik's file provider a moment to (re)load the dynamic config
   181:   ansible.builtin.wait_for:
   182:     timeout: 5
   183:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   184: 
   185: - name: Read the recent Traefik journal for file-provider errors
   186:   ansible.builtin.command:
   187:     cmd: journalctl -u traefik --no-pager --since "-30 seconds"
   188:   register: _traefik_journal
   189:   changed_when: false
   190:   failed_when: false
   191:   when: traefik_manage_services | bool
   192: 
   193: - name: Fail loudly if Traefik rejected the rendered dynamic config
   194:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   195:     that:
   196:       # "collecting file configs" is Traefik's wrapper for ANY file-provider
   197:       # config error (YAML parse, unknown key, ...); it never appears on a clean
   198:       # load, so its presence means the live routers were NOT updated.
   199:       - "'collecting file configs' not in _traefik_journal.stdout"
   200:     fail_msg: >-
   201:       Traefik's file provider REJECTED the rendered dynamic config — the live
   202:       routers are stale and every host behind Traefik will 404. Fix
   203:       dynamic.yml.j2 and re-converge. Recent journal:
   204:       {{ _traefik_journal.stdout_lines[-12:] | join('\n') }}
   205:     success_msg: "Traefik accepted the dynamic config (file provider loaded clean)."

   111:   failed_when: dns_server_freeze_result.rc != 0 and 'not found' not in dns_server_freeze_result.stderr
   112:   when: dns_server_need_zone_update and dns_server_container_running | bool

   125:     group: "{{ dns_server_uid }}"

   127:   when: dns_server_need_zone_update
   128: 
   129: - name: Reload and thaw zone in running DNS server
   130:   ansible.builtin.command:
   131:     cmd: "docker exec {{ dns_server_container_name }} rndc {{ item }} {{ dns_server_zone_name }}"
   132:   changed_when: true
   133:   loop:
   134:     - reload
   135:     - thaw
   136:   when: dns_server_need_zone_update and dns_server_container_running | bool

   141:   changed_when: true

name: playbooks/windows/provision_test_machine.yaml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact overly complex because several size and dependency dimensions compound?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Provision a Windows machine as a self-contained application test bed:
     3: # create a dedicated test user, install a configurable set of applications,
     4: # and (optionally) open Remote Desktop so an interactive agent can log in
     5: # and drive the GUI.
     6: #
     7: # Written for — but not limited to — Windows VMs running on OpenShift
     8: # Virtualization, where an automation agent later signs in as the test user
     9: # to exercise the installed applications. See README.md for how a fresh VM
    10: # gets its first WinRM/SSH listener (sysprep answer file or cloudbase-init);
    11: # this play takes over from the moment Ansible can connect.
    12: #
    13: # This play composes the building blocks shown in manage_local_users.yaml
    14: # and install_applications.yaml — read those two for the full option set.
    15: #
    16: # Targeting: pass ansible_limit=<host-or-group>. Defaults to the 'windows'
    17: # inventory group.
    18: #
    19: # Variables:
    20: #   windows_test_user           - test account to create (default 'apptester')
    21: #   windows_test_user_password  - REQUIRED. Pass via extra_vars, e.g.
    22: #                                 -e windows_test_user_password="{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword',
    23: #                                    'windows-apptester', field='password', vault='lab_agents') }}"
    24: #                                 Must satisfy the default Windows password
    25: #                                 complexity policy (length + character
    26: #                                 classes) or win_user rejects it and the
    27: #                                 play fails.
    28: #   windows_test_user_groups    - local groups for the account
    29: #                                 (default: Users + Remote Desktop Users)
    30: #   windows_test_apps           - Chocolatey packages to install; a list of
    31: #                                 dicts with name / version (optional) /
    32: #                                 state (optional, default present)
    33: #   windows_test_msi_packages   - extra MSI/EXE installers not available in
    34: #                                 Chocolatey; list of dicts with path (local
    35: #                                 path or URL), product_id, arguments,
    36: #                                 creates_path (see win_package docs).
    37: #                                 Default: none.
    38: #   windows_test_enable_rdp     - enable Remote Desktop + firewall rule so
    39: #                                 GUI agents can connect (default true)
    40: #
    41: # Run:
    42: #   ansible-navigator run playbooks/windows/provision_test_machine.yaml \
    43: #     -i igou-inventory/inventory.yaml -e ansible_limit=<vm-host> \
    44: #     -e windows_test_user_password=<secret>
    45: - name: Provision a Windows application test machine
    46:   hosts: "{{ ansible_limit | default('windows') }}"
    47:   gather_facts: false
    48: 
    49:   vars:
    50:     windows_test_user: apptester
    51:     windows_test_user_groups:
    52:       - Users
    53:       - Remote Desktop Users
    54:     windows_test_apps:
    55:       - name: git
    56:       - name: 7zip
    57:       - name: notepadplusplus
    58:     windows_test_msi_packages: []
    59:     windows_test_enable_rdp: true
    60: 
    61:   tasks:
    62:     # Fail fast with a clear message instead of a mid-play "undefined
    63:     # variable" error — passwords must come from extra_vars or a vault,
    64:     # never from a file checked into git.
    65:     - name: Make sure a password was provided for the test user
    66:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    67:         that:
    68:           - windows_test_user_password is defined
    69:           - windows_test_user_password | default('') | length > 0
    70:         fail_msg: >-
    71:           Set windows_test_user_password via extra_vars (ideally from a
    72:           1Password lookup) — see the header of this playbook.
    73: 
    74:     # --- Test user -------------------------------------------------------
    75:     # no_log hides the module arguments (which include the password) from
    76:     # logs and console output. update_password: on_create keeps the play
    77:     # idempotent — reruns won't reset a password the user already rotated.
    78:     - name: Create the application test user
    79:       ansible.windows.win_user:
    80:         name: "{{ windows_test_user }}"
    81:         password: "{{ windows_test_user_password }}"
    82:         update_password: on_create
    83:         password_never_expires: true
    84:         description: Application test account managed by Ansible
    85:         groups: "{{ windows_test_user_groups }}"
    86:         groups_action: add
    87:         state: present
    88:       no_log: true
    89: 
    90:     # --- Applications ----------------------------------------------------
    91:     # Chocolatey's bootstrap runs a downloaded .ps1, which the default
    92:     # execution policy on Windows CLIENT SKUs (Restricted) blocks — the
    93:     # bootstrap dies with "running scripts is disabled on this system".
    94:     # Ensure at least RemoteSigned (the Windows Server default, which
    95:     # permits locally-created unsigned scripts) at LocalMachine scope so
    96:     # the bootstrap can run. Idempotent: only writes when the policy is
    97:     # more restrictive than RemoteSigned/Unrestricted/Bypass. Same fix as
    98:     # install_applications.yaml.
    99:     - name: Ensure the execution policy permits the Chocolatey bootstrap
   100:       ansible.windows.win_shell: |
   101:         $ok = @('RemoteSigned', 'Unrestricted', 'Bypass')
   102:         if ((Get-ExecutionPolicy -Scope LocalMachine) -notin $ok) {
   103:           Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope LocalMachine -Force
   104:           'changed'
   105:         } else {
   106:           'ok'
   107:         }
   108:       register: windows_test_execpolicy
   109:       changed_when: "'changed' in windows_test_execpolicy.stdout"
   110: 
   111:     # The first win_chocolatey run bootstraps Chocolatey itself from the
   112:     # internet, so the VM needs outbound HTTPS (or set an internal source —
   113:     # see install_applications.yaml).
   114:     - name: Install test applications with Chocolatey
   115:       chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey:
   116:         name: "{{ item.name }}"
   117:         version: "{{ item.version | default(omit) }}"
   118:         state: "{{ item.state | default('present') }}"
   119:       loop: "{{ windows_test_apps }}"
   120:       loop_control:
   121:         label: "{{ item.name }}"
   122: 
   123:     # win_package handles anything Chocolatey can't: vendor MSIs, EXE
   124:     # installers from a share or URL. product_id is what makes reruns
   125:     # idempotent — without it (or creates_path) the installer runs again
   126:     # every time.
   127:     - name: Install extra MSI/EXE packages
   128:       ansible.windows.win_package:
   129:         path: "{{ item.path }}"
   130:         product_id: "{{ item.product_id | default(omit) }}"
   131:         arguments: "{{ item.arguments | default(omit) }}"
   132:         creates_path: "{{ item.creates_path | default(omit) }}"
   133:         state: present
   134:       loop: "{{ windows_test_msi_packages }}"
   135:       loop_control:
   136:         label: "{{ item.path }}"
   137: 
   138:     # --- Remote Desktop (optional) ----------------------------------------
   139:     # Three pieces make RDP reachable: the registry switch that allows
   140:     # connections, the service, and a firewall rule. The test user gets in
   141:     # because it is a member of "Remote Desktop Users" (see vars above).
   142:     - name: Allow Remote Desktop connections
   143:       ansible.windows.win_regedit:
   144:         path: HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server
   145:         name: fDenyTSConnections
   146:         data: 0
   147:         type: dword
   148:       when: windows_test_enable_rdp
   149: 
   150:     - name: Start the Remote Desktop service
   151:       ansible.windows.win_service:
   152:         name: TermService
   153:         start_mode: auto
   154:         state: started
   155:       when: windows_test_enable_rdp
   156: 
   157:     - name: Open the firewall for Remote Desktop
   158:       community.windows.win_firewall_rule:
   159:         name: Remote Desktop (managed by Ansible)
   160:         direction: in
   161:         action: allow
   162:         protocol: tcp
   163:         localport: "3389"
   164:         profiles:
   165:           - domain
   166:           - private
   167:           # Fresh workgroup/KubeVirt VMs classify the NIC as Public, so
   168:           # RDP stays blocked without this (lab-only; see README).
   169:           - public
   170:         state: present
   171:         enabled: true
   172:       when: windows_test_enable_rdp
   173: 
   174:     - name: Summarize what was provisioned
   175:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   176:         msg:
   177:           - "Test user:  {{ windows_test_user }} (groups: {{ windows_test_user_groups | join(', ') }})"
   178:           - "Apps:       {{ windows_test_apps | map(attribute='name') | join(', ') }}"
   179:           - "Extra pkgs: {{ windows_test_msi_packages | length }}"
   180:           - "RDP:        {{ 'enabled' if windows_test_enable_rdp else 'left as-is' }}"

    80: - name: "Determine Python executable for setting up virtualenev"

   133: - name: "Check if conda is already installed"
   134:   stat:
   135:     path: "{{ galaxy_tool_dependency_dir }}/_conda/bin/conda"

   137: 
   138: - name: "Prepare for reinstallation of conda"

   187: 
   188: - name: "Add environment setup file"

   190:     dest='{{ galaxy_dir }}/environment_setup.sh'
   191:     src='{{ galaxy_environment_setup_file }}'

   193: 
   194: - name: Create Galaxy configuration file
   195:   template:
   196:     dest='{{ galaxy_root }}/config/galaxy.yml'

   199: # Deal with possible bug when Galaxy installs Mercurial in

   201: - name: "Check for Galaxy Mercurial"

   203:     path: '{{ galaxy_root }}/.venv/bin/hg'

   219: 
   220: # Import or create tool_conf files
   221: - name: "Import base tool_conf.xml"

   264:

   266: - name: Create directory for chromosome length files
   267:   file:
   268:     path='{{ galaxy_root }}/tool-data/shared/ucsc/chrom'

   270:     mode='ugo+rX'

   273: - name: Create unknown chromosome length file

   282:   copy:

   285:     mode='ugo+r'
   286:   with_items: "{{ galaxy_chromosome_len_files }}"
   287:   when: galaxy_chromosome_len_files|default(None) != None
   288: 
   289: # Sanitization whitelist
   290: - name: Add tools to sanitization whitelist
   291:   lineinfile:
   292:     path='{{ galaxy_root }}/config/{{ galaxy_sanitize_whitelist_file }}'
   293:     state=present
   294:     create=yes
   295:     line="{{ item }}"
   296:   with_items: "{{ galaxy_sanitize_whitelist_tools }}"
   297:   when: galaxy_sanitize_whitelist_tools|default(None) != None
   298: 
   299: # Remove compiled .mako templates
   300: - name: "Remove compiled .mako templates from 'database'"
   301:   file:
   302:     path: '{{ galaxy_root }}/database/compiled_templates/'
   303:     state: absent
   304:   when: galaxy_remove_mako_templates == True

   307:   file:
   308:     path: '{{ galaxy_root }}/database/cache/compiled_templates/'
   309:     state: absent
   310:   when: galaxy_remove_mako_templates == True
   311: 
   312: # Temp dirs for pip and yarn caches
   313: - name: "Check/create temporary cache directory"
   314:   file:
   315:     path: "{{ galaxy_installation_tmp_dir }}"
   316:     state: directory
   317: 
   318: - name: "Make temporary pip cache directory"
   319:   tempfile:
   320:     path: "{{ galaxy_installation_tmp_dir }}"
   321:     prefix: "pip.cache."
   322:     state: directory
   323:   register: pip_cache_dir
   324: 
   325: - name: "Make temporary yarn cache directory"
   326:   tempfile:
   327:     path: "{{ galaxy_installation_tmp_dir }}"
   328:     prefix: "yarn.cache."
   329:     state: directory
   330:   register: yarn_cache_dir
   331: 
   332: # Setup/update Galaxy
   333: - name: "Run common_startup.sh to initialise/update Galaxy installation"

   339:     PIP_CACHE_DIR: '{{ pip_cache_dir.path }}'

   341: 
   342: # Create or update Galaxy database

   347: 
   348: - name: "Initialise Galaxy database"
   349:   block:
   350:     - name: "Create new (empty) Galaxy database"
   351:       command:
   352:         cmd: "./manage_db.sh init"
   353:         chdir: "{{ galaxy_root }}"

   355: 
   356:     - name: "Import external Galaxy database SQL file"
   357:       block:
   358:         - name: "Import existing Galaxy database from SQL file"
   359:           shell:
   360:             "PGPASSWORD={{ galaxy_db_password }} psql -U {{ galaxy_db_user }} {{ galaxy_db}} < {{ galaxy_new_db_sql }}"
   361: 
   362:         - name: "Upgrade the imported database schema"

   368: 
   369: - name: "Backup and upgrade existing Galaxy database"

   374: 
   375:     - name: "Upgrade the Galaxy database schema"

   378:         chdir: '{{ galaxy_root }}'
   379:   when: dbstatus.stdout != "No relations found." and dbstatus.stderr != "Did not find any relations."
   380: 
   381: # Run monitor script to write basic (static) status page

   394:   cron:
   395:     name: "{ galaxy_name }} generate static status page"

   397:   when: galaxy_generate_status_page == False

1: ---
     2: # ClusterServiceVersion resource uses a different API.
     3: - name: Get all resources from namespace
     4:   kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
     5:     api_version: "\
     6:       {% if resources.resource == 'ClusterServiceVersion' %}\
     7:         operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1\
     8:       {% else %}\
     9:         v1\
    10:       {% endif %}"
    11:     namespace: "{{ resources.namespace }}"
    12:     kind: "{{ resources.resource }}"
    13:   register: resources_in_ns
    14: 
    15: # We only want to handle resources without ownerReferences, just to avoid
    16: # duplicating components.
    17: - name: Check ownerReferences for the retrieved resources
    18:   block:
    19:     - name: "Getting resources details"
    20:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    21:         resource_details: "{{ resources_in_ns | json_query(details_query) }}"  # noqa: jinja[invalid]
    22:       vars:
    23:         details_query: >
    24:           resources[*].{ kind: kind,
    25:             name: metadata.name,
    26:             owner: metadata.ownerReferences,
    27:             spec: spec
    28:           }
    29: 
    30:     - name: "Filtering resources with no ownerReferences"
    31:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    32:         resource_details: "{{ resource_details | json_query(filter_query) }}"  # noqa: jinja[invalid]
    33:       vars:
    34:         filter_query: "[?owner == null]"
    35: 
    36:     - name: Print resources to be inspected
    37:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    38:         msg: "{{ resource_details }}"
    39: 
    40: # Depending on the resource type, the way of extracting the images is
    41: # different.  ReplicaSet, StatefulSet and Deployment work in the same way, so
    42: # they are covered with the else statement.
    43: - name: Extract container images from resources
    44:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    45:     container_images_in_ns: "\
    46:       {% if resources.resource == 'Pod' %}\
    47:         {{ resource_details | json_query('[*].spec.containers[*].image') | flatten | unique }}\
    48:       {% elif resources.resource == 'ClusterServiceVersion' %}\
    49:         {{ resource_details | json_query('[*].spec.relatedImages[*].image') | flatten | unique }}\
    50:       {% else %}\
    51:         {{ resource_details | json_query('[*].spec.template.spec.containers[*].image') | flatten | unique }}\
    52:       {% endif %}"
    53: 
    54: # Then, create the component, and that's the same for all resources.
    55: # Why we do this in this way?
    56: #
    57: # * container_image_without_version
    58: #   if image does not use digest
    59: #     if image has a tag
    60: #       - remove tag
    61: #     else
    62: #       - use the same container_image as it does not have tag (or digest)
    63: #   else
    64: #     - remove digest
    65: # * container_image_name
    66: #   - taking container_image_without_version, remove the registry
    67: # * container_image_version
    68: #   if image does not use digest
    69: #     if image has a tag
    70: #       - take the tag
    71: #     else
    72: #       - use "latest" as tag
    73: #   else
    74: #     - take the digest
    75: # * container_image_version_short
    76: #   shorten container_image_version if it uses digest; just take the 7 first chars.
    77: #   To be used in the component displayed name.
    78: # If we try to create a component that already exists, it will not be created.
    79: - name: Create a component based on resource information
    80:   vars:
    81:     container_image_without_version: "\
    82:       {% if container_image.split('@') | length == 1 %}\
    83:         {% if '/' not in container_image.split(':')[-1] %}\
    84:           {% for image_chunk in container_image.split(':') %}\
    85:             {% if not loop.last %}\
    86:               {{ image_chunk }}{% if loop.index < loop.length - 1 %}:{% endif %}\
    87:             {% endif %}\
    88:           {% endfor %}\
    89:         {% else %}\
    90:           {{ container_image }}\
    91:         {% endif %}\
    92:       {% else %}\
    93:         {% for image_chunk in container_image.split('@') %}\
    94:           {% if not loop.last %}\
    95:             {{ image_chunk }}{% if loop.index < loop.length - 1 %}@{% endif %}\
    96:           {% endif %}\
    97:         {% endfor %}\
    98:       {% endif %}"
    99:     container_image_name: "\
   100:       {% for image_chunk in container_image_without_version.split('/') %}\
   101:         {% if loop.index > 1 %}{{ image_chunk }}{% if not loop.last %}/{% endif %}{% endif %}\
   102:       {% endfor %}"
   103:     container_image_version: "\
   104:       {% if container_image.split('@') | length == 1 %}\
   105:         {% if '/' not in container_image.split(':')[-1] %}\
   106:           {{ container_image.split(':')[-1] }}\
   107:         {% else %}\
   108:           latest
   109:         {% endif %}\
   110:       {% else %}\
   111:         {{ container_image.split('@')[-1] }}\
   112:       {% endif %}"
   113:     container_image_version_short: "\
   114:       {% if container_image_version.split(':') | length == 1 %}\
   115:         {{ container_image_version }}\
   116:       {% else %}\
   117:         {{ container_image_version.split(':')[-1][:7] }}\
   118:       {% endif %}"
   119:     comp_display_name: "IMG {{ container_image_name }} {{ container_image_version_short }}"
   120:     comp_version: "{{ container_image_version }}"
   121:     comp_type: "{{ container_image_name }}"
   122:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: create-component.yml
   123:   loop: "{{ container_images_in_ns }}"
   124:   loop_control:
   125:     loop_var: container_image
   126: ...

    97:     # `core.lifecycle_canonical._zeroclaw_install_slack_mcp`. This

   126:     - name: Remove legacy clawctl dropin (Bundle 5 #510 rename migration)
   127:       ansible.builtin.file:
   128:         path: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service.d/10-clm-env.conf"

   130:       no_log: true

   134:     # [Service] block when no github integrations are assigned — systemd
   135:     # treats that as a no-op overlay. Mode 0600 because the file contains
   136:     # the GITHUB_TOKEN verbatim (read-only to root; systemd is started as
   137:     # root so this is fine). notify the restart handler so the drop-in is

   141:         src: "{{ template_path }}/zeroclaw-env.conf.j2"

   143:         owner: root
   144:         group: root
   145:         mode: "0600"
   146:         force: yes
   147:       no_log: true
   148:       notify: Restart zeroclaw service

   150:     # #649: github + git integration wiring moved to the canonical sync
   151:     # pipeline (`core/lifecycle_canonical.py:_setup_github_integration`).
   152:     # Fires on every `clawctl agent sync` when a `git` or `github`
   153:     # integration is attached, agent-type-agnostic. configure.yaml is
   154:     # not invoked by the modern kubectl-style CLI, so keeping the
   155:     # legacy `Render ~/.gitconfig` + `GitHub CLI authentication block`
   156:     # here was dead code — same class of bug as #755 / #834 (openclaw
   157:     # brave / hermes slack MCP install moved out of configure.yaml).

   160:     # probe so /health is observing the just-rendered config, not the
   161:     # previous incarnation.
   162:     - name: Apply pending restart before probing
   163:       ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers

   165:     - name: Start zeroclaw service
   166:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   167:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"

   171:     # 30×2s of /health retries (ATX W4). ActiveState may be `activating`
   172:     # momentarily; accept that as in-progress and let the health probe
   173:     # finish the wait.
   174:     - name: Verify zeroclaw service did not crash on startup
   175:       ansible.builtin.command:
   176:         cmd: "systemctl show -p ActiveState --value {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
   177:       register: service_state
   178:       changed_when: false
   179:       failed_when: service_state.stdout.strip() in ['failed', 'inactive']

   181:     # Wait for the daemon to come up. /health/providers is the canonical
   182:     # readiness signal — it 200s only after the provider config has been
   183:     # parsed and the gateway is listening. Accept 401 too because the
   184:     # endpoint may require pairing-auth before serving — the existence of
   185:     # a response means the gateway is up.
   186:     - name: Probe /health/providers
   187:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   188:         url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/health/providers"
   189:         method: GET

   192:       register: health_probe
   193:       retries: 30
   194:       delay: 2
   195:       until: health_probe.status in [200, 401]

   197:       # the playbook's `no_log: true` hygiene. The probe body itself is
   198:       # non-secret but the registered `health_probe` is later used in
   199:       # `set_fact` branches gated on `status` — suppress to keep the
   200:       # log surface tight at high verbosity.
   201:       no_log: true
   202: 
   203:     # ATX Round 1 W3 + Round 2 W1 + Round 3 W1: surface a non-fatal
   204:     # warning when /health/providers returns 401. The gateway is up but
   205:     # the provider credentials probably mismatch the API key supplied in
   206:     # config.toml — chat calls will fail at request time.

   212:     # propagates through the same fact-cache path the bearer token uses.

   214:     # Round 3 W1: assign the literal boolean unconditionally so a healthy
   215:     # run (status 200) clears any stale `true` left over from a prior
   216:     # 401 — `cacheable: true` would otherwise keep the previous value
   217:     # persisted in Ansible's fact cache and emit a phantom warning on
   218:     # every subsequent configure.

   220:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:

   226:         msg: >-
   227:           /health/providers returned 401 — gateway is reachable but
   228:           provider credentials may be invalid. Verify the API key for
   229:           provider '{{ config.provider.type }}' and re-run
   230:           `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` if needed.

   233:     # Always re-pair (issue #437). The daemon does not persist bearer
   234:     # state across restarts, so the only way to make hosts.json
   235:     # structurally agree with the daemon is to mint a fresh token on
   236:     # every configure run. The trade-off (in-flight `clawctl agent chat` sessions

   238:     # eliminating the silent divergence class entirely.
   239:     - name: Run zeroclaw pair handshake
   240:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/pair.yaml
   241: 
   242:     # Discord-config verification (#422). Confirms the bot token + an
   243:     # allowlist landed in config.toml when Discord is enabled. grep -q so
   244:     # we get a clean exit status without leaking the rendered key into logs.
   245:     # Uses dict.get() pattern (not attribute access) so undefined keys
   246:     # don't error under Ansible 2.20+'s strict Jinja mode.

   248:       ansible.builtin.command:
   249:         cmd: grep -qE '^bot_token\s*=' "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/config.toml"

   251:       changed_when: false
   252:       failed_when: discord_token_check.rc != 0

   254:       when:
   255:         - config.channels is defined
   256:         - config.channels.discord is defined
   257:         - config.channels.discord.enabled | default(false)

   259:     # Autonomy block always renders, so the grep is unconditional. This
   260:     # catches a Jinja regression that drops the block (which would silently
   261:     # disable shell_env_passthrough → tools lose GITHUB_TOKEN, _SECRET, etc.).
   262:     - name: Verify config.toml renders [autonomy] block with shell_env_passthrough
   263:       ansible.builtin.command:
   264:         cmd: grep -qE '^shell_env_passthrough\s*=' "/home/{{ agent_name }}/.zeroclaw/config.toml"
   265:       register: autonomy_check
   266:       changed_when: false
   267:       failed_when: autonomy_check.rc != 0
   268: 
   269:     - name: Display configure success
   270:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   271:         msg: |
   272:           ZeroClaw agent '{{ agent_name }}' configured with provider
   273:           '{{ config.provider.type }}'.
   274:           Pairing: fresh token minted (issue #437 — every lifecycle op re-pairs).

   276: 
   277:   handlers:
   278:     # Single canonical restart handler. daemon_reload covers config-file
   279:     # changes that don't touch the unit, and the same restart fires once per
   280:     # configure regardless of how many notify directives match.
   281:     - name: Restart zeroclaw service
   282:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   283:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Purpose: Deploys ClusterForge platform
     3: # Dependencies: CLUSTERFORGE_REPO, CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE, DOMAIN variables
     4: # Usage: Imported by main cluster-bloom.yaml playbook
     5: # Tags: [deploy_clusterforge]
     6: 
     7: - name: Validate ClusterForge bootstrap parameters
     8:   assert:
     9:     that:
    10:       - FIRST_NODE is defined
    11:       - FIRST_NODE | bool
    12:       - DOMAIN is defined and DOMAIN != ""
    13:     fail_msg: "deploy_clusterforge requires FIRST_NODE: true and DOMAIN"
    14:     success_msg: "✓ ClusterForge bootstrap parameters provided"
    15:   when:
    16:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE is defined
    17:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE != "none"
    18:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE != ""
    19:   tags: [clusterforge, deploy_clusterforge]
    20: 
    21: # Nodes are joined first with CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE "none", so a node whose
    22: # Longhorn CSI plugin never came up stays latent — it looks Ready and nothing
    23: # demands a volume from it — until ClusterForge is deployed days later. The
    24: # failure then surfaces as a five-minute `kubectl wait` timeout on
    25: # openbao-init-job, four layers above the actual cause. Checking CSI driver
    26: # registration up front names the bad node instead.
    27: - name: Verify every node has registered the Longhorn CSI driver
    28:   shell: |
    29:     set -o pipefail
    30:     KUBECTL="/var/lib/rancher/rke2/bin/kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/rancher/rke2/rke2.yaml"
    31:     nodes=$($KUBECTL get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}')
    32:     # Without this the check passes vacuously: a kubectl failure yields an empty
    33:     # list, the loop below never runs, and an unchecked cluster reports success.
    34:     if [ -z "$nodes" ]; then
    35:       echo "Could not list nodes to verify Longhorn CSI registration"
    36:       exit 1
    37:     fi
    38:     missing=""
    39:     for node in $nodes; do
    40:       drivers=$($KUBECTL get csinode "$node" -o jsonpath='{.spec.drivers[*].name}' 2>/dev/null)
    41:       case " $drivers " in
    42:         *" driver.longhorn.io "*) ;;
    43:         *) missing="$missing $node" ;;
    44:       esac
    45:     done
    46:     if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
    47:       echo "Nodes missing driver.longhorn.io:$missing"
    48:       exit 1
    49:     fi
    50:     echo "All nodes have registered driver.longhorn.io"
    51:   args:
    52:     executable: /bin/bash
    53:   register: longhorn_csinode_check
    54:   until: longhorn_csinode_check.rc == 0
    55:   retries: 30
    56:   delay: 10
    57:   changed_when: false
    58:   failed_when: false
    59:   when:
    60:     - FIRST_NODE | default(true) | bool
    61:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE is defined
    62:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE != "none"
    63:     - CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE != ""
    64:     - CLUSTER_SIZE == "large"
    65:     - not (NO_DISKS_FOR_CLUSTER | default(false) | bool)
    66:   tags: [clusterforge, longhorn, deploy_clusterforge]
    67: 
    68: - name: Fail when a node cannot serve Longhorn volumes
    69:   fail:
    70:     msg: |
    71:       {{ longhorn_csinode_check.stdout | trim }}
    72: 
    73:       Any pod with a Longhorn PVC scheduled onto those nodes will hang in
    74:       ContainerCreating with "CSINode <node> does not contain driver
    75:       driver.longhorn.io", and ClusterForge will fail later with an
    76:       unrelated-looking timeout.
    77: 
    78:       Check the CSI plugin on the affected node:
    79:         kubectl -n longhorn get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
    80: 
    81:       If longhorn-csi-plugin is CrashLoopBackOff with "Failed to initialize
    82:       Longhorn API client ... context deadline exceeded", its pod sandbox has a
    83:       dead network namespace. Restarting the container cannot fix that — the
    84:       sandbox must be recreated:
    85:         kubectl -n longhorn delete pod <longhorn-csi-plugin-pod>
    86:   when:
    87:     - longhorn_csinode_check.rc is defined
    88:     - longhorn_csinode_check.rc != 0
    89:   tags: [clusterforge, longhorn, deploy_clusterforge]
    90: 
    91: - name: Build DISABLED_APPS from AIWB_ONLY flag

    10: - name: Ensure media-repo paths exist
    11:   ansible.builtin.file:
    12:     path: "{{ item.path }}"
    13:     state: directory
    14:     mode: '0750'
    15:     owner: "{{ matrix_user_name }}"

    17:   with_items:
    18:     - path: "{{ matrix_media_repo_base_path }}"

    21:       when: true
    22:     - path: "{{ matrix_media_repo_data_path }}"
    23:       when: true
    24:     - path: "{{ matrix_media_repo_container_src_files_path }}"
    25:       when: "{{ matrix_media_repo_container_image_self_build }}"
    26:   when: "item.when | bool"
    27: 
    28: - name: Ensure media-repo support files installed
    29:   ansible.builtin.template:
    30:     src: "{{ role_path }}/templates/media-repo/{{ item }}.j2"
    31:     dest: "{{ matrix_media_repo_base_path }}/{{ item }}"
    32:     mode: '0640'
    33:     owner: "{{ matrix_user_name }}"
    34:     group: "{{ matrix_group_name }}"
    35:   with_items:
    36:     - env
    37:     - labels
    38:   register: matrix_media_repo_support_files_result
    39: 
    40: - name: Ensure media-repo configuration installed
    41:   ansible.builtin.template:
    42:     src: "{{ role_path }}/templates/media-repo/media-repo.yaml.j2"
    43:     dest: "{{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }}/media-repo.yaml"
    44:     mode: '0640'
    45:     owner: "{{ matrix_user_name }}"
    46:     group: "{{ matrix_group_name }}"
    47:   register: matrix_media_repo_config_result
    48: 
    49: - name: Ensure media-repo Docker image is pulled
    50:   community.docker.docker_image_pull:
    51:     name: "{{ matrix_media_repo_container_image }}"
    52:     pull: always
    53:   when: "not matrix_media_repo_container_image_self_build | bool"
    54:   register: matrix_media_repo_container_image_pull_result
    55:   retries: "{{ devture_playbook_help_container_retries_count }}"
    56:   delay: "{{ devture_playbook_help_container_retries_delay }}"
    57:   until: matrix_media_repo_container_image_pull_result is not failed
    58: 
    59: - when: "matrix_media_repo_container_image_self_build | bool"
    60:   block:
    61:     # A checkout owned by a different user (a uid change, an earlier clone by another user, etc.) would make the git task below fail on ownership or permissions.
    62:     - name: Ensure media-repo repository ownership is correct on self-build
    63:       ansible.builtin.file:
    64:         path: "{{ matrix_media_repo_container_src_files_path }}"
    65:         state: directory
    66:         owner: "{{ matrix_user_name }}"
    67:         group: "{{ matrix_group_name }}"
    68:         recurse: true
    69: 
    70:     - name: Ensure media-repo repository is present on self-build
    71:       ansible.builtin.git:
    72:         repo: "{{ matrix_media_repo_container_image_self_build_repo }}"
    73:         dest: "{{ matrix_media_repo_container_src_files_path }}"
    74:         version: "{{ matrix_media_repo_container_image.split(':')[1] }}"
    75:         force: "yes"
    76:       become: true
    77:       become_user: "{{ matrix_user_name }}"
    78:       register: matrix_media_repo_git_pull_results
    79: 
    80:     - name: Check if media-repo Docker image exists
    81:       ansible.builtin.command: "{{ devture_systemd_docker_base_host_command_docker }} images --quiet --filter 'reference={{ matrix_media_repo_container_image }}'"
    82:       register: matrix_media_repo_container_image_check_result
    83:       changed_when: false
    84: 
    85:     # Invoking the `docker build` command here, instead of calling the `docker_image` Ansible module,
    86:     # because the latter does not support BuildKit.
    87:     # See: https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.general/issues/514
    88:     - name: Ensure media-repo Docker image is built
    89:       ansible.builtin.command:
    90:         cmd: "{{ devture_systemd_docker_base_host_command_docker }} build -t {{ matrix_media_repo_container_image }} {{ matrix_media_repo_container_src_files_path }}"
    91:       environment:
    92:         DOCKER_BUILDKIT: 1
    93:       changed_when: true
    94:       when: "matrix_media_repo_git_pull_results.changed | bool or matrix_media_repo_container_image_check_result.stdout == ''"
    95: 
    96: - name: Check existence of media-repo signing key
    97:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    98:     path: "{{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }}/{{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}.signing.key"
    99:   register: matrix_media_repo_signing_key_stat
   100: 
   101: - when: "matrix_media_repo_generate_signing_key | bool and not (matrix_media_repo_signing_key_stat.stat.exists | bool)"
   102:   block:
   103:     - name: Generate media-repo signing key
   104:       ansible.builtin.command:
   105:         cmd: |
   106:           {{ devture_systemd_docker_base_host_command_docker }} run
   107:           --rm
   108:           --name={{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}-temp
   109:           --user={{ matrix_synapse_uid }}:{{ matrix_synapse_gid }}
   110:           --cap-drop=ALL
   111:           --mount type=bind,src={{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }},dst=/config
   112:           --workdir='/config'
   113:           --entrypoint='generate_signing_key'
   114:           {{ matrix_media_repo_container_image }}
   115:           -output {{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}.signing.key.TEMP
   116:         creates: "{{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }}/{{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}.signing.key.TEMP"
   117: 
   118:     - name: Merge media-repo signing key with homeserver signing key
   119:       ansible.builtin.command:
   120:         cmd: |
   121:           {{ devture_systemd_docker_base_host_command_docker }} run
   122:           --rm
   123:           --name={{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}-temp
   124:           --user={{ matrix_synapse_uid }}:{{ matrix_synapse_gid }}
   125:           --cap-drop=ALL
   126:           --mount type=bind,src={{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }},dst=/config
   127:           --mount type=bind,src={{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key | dirname }},dst=/homeserver-signing-key-dir
   128:           --workdir='/config'
   129:           --entrypoint='combine_signing_keys'
   130:           {{ matrix_media_repo_container_image }}
   131:           -format {{ matrix_homeserver_implementation }} -output /homeserver-signing-key-dir/{{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key | basename }}.merged /homeserver-signing-key-dir/{{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key | basename }} {{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}.signing.key.TEMP
   132:         creates: "{{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key }}.merged"

   135:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   136:         remote_src: true
   137:         src: "{{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key }}"
   138:         dest: "{{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key }}.{{ matrix_homeserver_implementation }}.backup"
   139:         mode: '0644'
   140:         owner: "{{ matrix_user_name }}"
   141:         group: "{{ matrix_group_name }}"

   143:     - name: Replace homeserver signing key with merged signing key
   144:       ansible.builtin.command:
   145:         cmd: "mv {{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key }}.merged {{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key }}"
   146:         removes: "{{ matrix_media_repo_homeserver_signing_key }}.merged"

   149:       ansible.builtin.command:
   150:         cmd: "mv {{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }}/{{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}.signing.key.TEMP {{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }}/{{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}.signing.key"
   151:         removes: "{{ matrix_media_repo_config_path }}/{{ matrix_media_repo_identifier }}.signing.key.TEMP"
